style: Approved light editorial illustrations on fixed white
typography: Helvetica Neue regular; Helvetica and Arial fallbacks

figures.alt_text: The room-booking website leads to the purpose of reliable access to suitable rooms. That purpose also leads to clearer descriptions, standing allocations, and drop-in space.
figures.caption: Ask what booking makes possible, then return through other ways to provide suitable space. The alternatives still need to meet the same requirements.
figures.rationale: The branches make the move from one implementation to a purpose and back through alternative implementations visible.

figures.alt_text: Three dimensions each offer two choices: setting, encounter, and contribution. Walking route, audio excerpts, and remembered places combine into a listening trail; the kitchen-table combination becomes a conversation pack.
figures.caption: Choose one alternative from each dimension, then describe and check the combination. The listening trail and conversation pack differ in their underlying arrangement.
figures.rationale: Aligned alternatives and complete combinations make recombination concrete without pretending to enumerate every possible design.

figures.alt_text: Six thinking jobs connect the courtyard concern to a trial: understand use, describe success, frame a question, generate options, develop a proposal, and align resources. A dashed return from the storage question reopens development.
figures.caption: The courtyard proposal moves through six different thinking jobs. If storage is unavailable, return to development instead of treating the plan as settled.
figures.rationale: The figure distinguishes thinking jobs and makes the return from a resource discovery to solution development explicit.

figures.alt_text: One concern, always being behind, branches into work arriving faster than it can finish and one request type blocking the rest. Each frame points to a different observation.
figures.caption: Both frames retain the backlog concern. One asks for incoming and completed work; the other asks where work waits. These checks can refine either interpretation.
figures.rationale: The branches pair each interpretation with its distinct check, showing why a wording change alone is insufficient.

figures.alt_text: The concern that meetings run too long leads to two moves. Exploration inspects which agenda item expands; breaking the frame asks which decisions need a live meeting at all.
figures.caption: Exploring keeps the meeting as the setting and investigates variation. Breaking questions whether the decisions need to be synchronous. Either move may be useful.
figures.rationale: A paired comparison holds the concern constant while distinguishing a closer investigation from a changed premise.

figures.alt_text: A timeline places changing expectations and urgent requests before a missed deadline. After it, anticipated criticism may delay the next warning. The expectation is marked as a hypothesis.
figures.caption: Widen the time window around the missed deadline. Sequence is not proof of cause: check both the earlier demands and the person’s account of the anticipated response.
figures.rationale: The timeline separates the visible episode from nearby events and from an inferred expectation.

figures.alt_text: A promotion branches into income, responsibility, and recognition. Each branch points to a different possible purpose: financial security, consequential work, and feeling valued.
figures.caption: Keep the branches distinct. A route that increases income may not provide responsibility or recognition; the person decides which purposes fit their experience.
figures.rationale: The tree preserves multiple legitimate purposes instead of collapsing the goal into a single inferred motive.

figures.alt_text: The proposed chain links more meetings to better communication to fewer mistakes. Under each arrow is a question: are decisions recorded, and which mistakes involve missing information?
figures.caption: The arrows are assumptions to examine. Recording decisions or clarifying ownership may matter more than adding meetings; the chain alone cannot settle that.
figures.rationale: Separate questions attached to each causal link distinguish the intended outcome from the proposed mechanism.

figures.alt_text: A release is connected to developers implementing, a product owner changing scope, reviewers approving, support handling defects, and customers waiting. The labels describe roles rather than assign blame.
figures.caption: Map what each group does or experiences before deciding where the delay originates. A role map suggests people to consult; it does not establish the cause.
figures.rationale: A spatial map restores omitted roles and makes the difference between responsibility and causal blame visible.

figures.alt_text: The same shipping crate is drawn as a storage container and as a possible raised display surface. The new use relies on its shape and stiffness and still requires a stability check.
figures.caption: Look beyond the label “storage.” A crate may provide a raised surface, but its strength and stability need checking before it becomes part of a stall.
figures.rationale: The same concrete object in two uses shows how a functional label can hide useful properties.

figures.alt_text: Vendor A, Vendor B, and an internal dashboard share the assumption of preserving a report. Other options question whether to simplify, partly automate, or retire the report.
figures.caption: The first group varies the implementation while retaining the report. The second changes the underlying account of what work is needed. Relevance still matters more than novelty.
figures.rationale: Grouping choices by their shared premise makes structural diversity visible.

figures.alt_text: Two simplified event entrance plans compare one host dividing attention between a visitor, a list, and a waiting person with two roles: initial contact and booking lookup. A separate map and queue marker are added in the second scene.
figures.caption: The second scene redistributes attention and clarifies waiting. Acting it out can expose new exceptions; the arrangement has not yet been validated with real visitors.
figures.rationale: A concrete plan comparison makes attention, roles, and physical arrangement visible in the same welcome-desk case.

figures.alt_text: A wordless drawing places one person between two blocks. A revised drawing shows people within both blocks and several possible connections. Tentative interpretations sit outside the drawings.
figures.caption: Changing scale and relationships can open a question about connecting work. The viewer’s interpretation remains tentative, and the artist can correct or reject it.
figures.rationale: The paired drawings demonstrate the change of representation while keeping interpretations outside the wordless image.

figures.alt_text: The same observation, few members speaking, is viewed through five possible frames: turn-taking, the opening question, discussion climate, the purpose of the gathering, and participation conditions. Each points to a different inquiry.
figures.caption: Keep the observation constant while changing the account. These five frames suggest different questions; they are hypotheses to examine, and several may overlap.
figures.rationale: The comparison demonstrates five structurally different interpretations and the different inquiry each opens.
